fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`import rebar` callers get a return value, not a terminal, so the first-class way to raise a
non-fatal warning is Python's **`warnings`** subsystem (not `logging`, which the brainstorm
rejected). This story emits a `warnings.warn` of a dedicated category from single-ticket
library functions when the detector fires. Depends on the merged detector
(`cross_session_warning_for`) and reducer clearing: a ticket not `in_progress` has no holder,
so the detector returns `None` and nothing is emitted.

## Approach

Add a new module `src/rebar/_lib_warn.py` defining `class CrossSessionWarning(UserWarning)`
and a best-effort helper `emit_cross_session_warning(ticket_id, *, repo_root=None)`, and
re-export the category as `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` so callers can filter/escalate it.
The module also exposes a `suppress_cross_session_warning()` context manager (holds the same
guard) so an outer surface that already advises stops the library channel from doubling it.

The helper mirrors the CLI's `_maybe_warn_cross_session`: it calls the merged detector
`cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` and, on a non-`None` string,
calls `warnings.warn(msg, CrossSessionWarning)`; on `None` it does nothing. Two properties:

- **Best-effort — never breaks the call.** The body is wrapped in
  `try/except Exception: pass`; the operation always proceeds, no warning on failure.
- **Re-entrancy-guarded.** The detector (`_commands/cross_session.py`) itself calls public
  `show_ticket`, so a naive emit on `show_ticket` would recurse. A module-level
  `contextvars.ContextVar` (`_EMITTING`, default `False`) makes the helper a no-op while an
  emit is in progress (returns if set, else sets/runs/resets in `finally`), so exactly one
  warning fires per top-level call. The detector is **not** modified.

Each single-ticket public entry point calls
`emit_cross_session_warning(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` **before** returning (for writes,
before the mutation, so the holder is read pre-mutation — matching CLI/MCP). **No return type
changes.** Covered public functions (from `src/rebar/__init__.py`) are enumerated per file in
Scope; `quality_check` is **out of scope** — absent from the CLI allowlist, deferred on MCP
(S4).

`link`/`unlink` warn for the **primary endpoint `id1`** only, matching CLI (S3)/MCP (S4).
Bulk reads (`list_tickets`, `search`, `ready`, `next_batch`) do **not** warn. `claim` raises
`ConcurrencyError` on an `in_progress` ticket before any warning path.
### Surface layering (single-emit dedup)

The CLI and MCP surfaces call these same library functions, so a naive library emit doubles
the advisory each already carries (CLI stderr `WARN:`; MCP `cross_session_warning` field).
Dedup keeps exactly one advisory per operation per surface:

- **CLI** (`src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py`) — `execute()` runs `_maybe_warn_cross_session` (the
  allowlist single source) **and** handler dispatch inside `suppress_cross_session_warning()`,
  so the library `CrossSessionWarning` is suppressed and the CLI's `WARN:` line is the only
  CLI advisory.
- **MCP** (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py`) — `build_server()` registers read/write tools through
  `suppress_library_double_advisory(mcp)` (in `_lib_warn.py`), a proxy that runs each tool
  handler (sync + `async`) inside `suppress_cross_session_warning()`, so the response field is
  the only MCP advisory WITHOUT a process-global filter (which would over-silence the library
  `CrossSessionWarning` for unrelated `import rebar` callers sharing the server process).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_lib_warn.py` (**new**) — `CrossSessionWarning(UserWarning)`, best-effort
  re-entrancy-guarded `emit_cross_session_warning`, `suppress_cross_session_warning`, and the
  `suppress_library_double_advisory(mcp)` MCP proxy (scopes suppression per tool handler).
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` — re-export `CrossSessionWarning` (import + `__all__`).
- `src/rebar/_lib_reads.py` — emit in `show_ticket`, `deps`.
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — emit in `transition` (before the mutation); `reopen`
  delegates to it, so it does not emit separately (no double warning).
- `src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py` — emit in `comment`, `edit_ticket`, `link` (`id1`),
  `unlink` (`id1`), `tag`, `untag`, `archive`.
- `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` — emit in `set_file_impact`, `declare_no_file_impact`,
  `clarity_check`, `check_ac`. `quality_check` out of scope (see Approach).
- `src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py` — hold `suppress_cross_session_warning()` across detection +
  dispatch so the library never doubles the CLI `WARN:` line.
- `src/rebar/mcp_server.py` — `build_server()` wraps read/write tool registration with the
  `suppress_library_double_advisory` proxy (scoped per-handler suppression; no global filter).
- `src/rebar/_commands/cross_session.py` — `cross_session_warning_for` reads the config toggle
  and acting session BEFORE the `show_ticket` reduce, short-circuiting (skipping the reduce and
  cache write) when the feature is disabled or the session is unknown.
- `docs/reuse-surface.md` — document `rebar.CrossSessionWarning`.
- `tests/unit/test_cross_session_lib.py` (**new**) — the library-surface oracle.
- `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json` — refresh for the new `CrossSessionWarning` export.
- `tests/unit/test_fold_orphan_laundering.py` — exclude the reducer `.cache.json` dotfile
  from event-file enumeration (library mutations now reduce for the holder pre-check, which
  persists the cache — matches `graph/_cache.py`).

## Testing

Tier: **in-process unit test** with stdlib `warnings` capture (`pytest.warns` /
`catch_warnings(record=True)`). Real temporary tracker; acting session via `REBAR_SESSION_ID`
(monkeypatch). Claim as holder A, then act as B.

- B vs A-held: `show_ticket` and `comment` each emit one warning naming A; write applies.
- Write + two-endpoint: `transition` and `link` (holder A on `id1`) each emit one for `id1`.
- Negative control (same session A): none. Bulk (`list_tickets`/`ready` as B): none.
- Unset `REBAR_SESSION_ID`: none. Category is `isinstance(..., CrossSessionWarning)`.
- Re-entrancy: exactly one per top-level `show_ticket`. Best-effort: detector raises -> call
  returns, no warning. Per-site sweep: each instrumented fn emits exactly one (0=missed,
  2=double); reopen delegates to transition (one). CLI dedup: one `WARN:` per command.
  Defect-seeded: negate guard / wrong endpoint -> RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` and `rebar.comment(<id>, ...)`, as B vs an A-held ticket, each
  emit exactly one `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` naming holder `A` (`pytest.warns` under
  `make test`); the `comment` write still applies.
- [x] `rebar.transition(<id>, "in_progress", "closed")` and `rebar.link(<id1>, <id2>, ...)`
  (endpoint `id1`), as B vs A-held `id1`, each emit one `CrossSessionWarning` naming `A`.
- [x] Same-session A negative control emits none; `list_tickets()`/`ready()` as B emit none.
- [x] With `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset, `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` emits none.
- [x] The emitted warning is `isinstance(..., rebar.CrossSessionWarning)` (subclass of
  `UserWarning`).
- [x] Re-entrancy: one `CrossSessionWarning` per top-level `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` despite
  the detector's internal read (recorded count for that category is 1).
- [x] Best-effort: when `cross_session_warning_for` raises, the library call returns normally
  and emits no `CrossSessionWarning` (monkeypatch-to-raise).
- [x] Single-emit dedup: a warning CLI command (e.g. `link`) writes exactly one `WARN:` line,
  not doubled by the library channel (`test_cross_session_cli.py` `count(...) == 1`).
- [x] `docs/reuse-surface.md` documents `rebar.CrossSessionWarning`
  (`grep -n "CrossSessionWarning" docs/reuse-surface.md` matches).
